notes: Outcome: no working RNLI feed address could be confirmed from here, so 'not-found'; keep rnli-news enabled or disabled as the maintainers prefer, but the 403 is not explained by robots.txt. What was established: (1) https://rnli.org/news-and-media/rss is not linked from the News and media page, its head, or the Latest lifeboat launches page, and the site offers no RSS, Atom, subscribe or feed link; the address in watch/sources.json therefore rests on earlier knowledge, not on anything the site advertises today. (2) rnli.org/robots.txt (User-agent: *) has no rule matching /news-and-media/rss; its only feed rule is 'Disallow: /*?feed='. The file also lists /cdn-cgi/ and ?__cf_chl_tk= paths, which are Cloudflare's, so the site sits behind Cloudflare; a Cloudflare bot rule answering 403 to non-browser user agents or to cloud-runner addresses is the likely mechanism, but that is a judgment (grade D), untested from here. (3) The fetch tool, which presents a browser-like client, was itself refused today with ROBOTS_DISALLOWED although robots.txt allows the path; an X-Robots-Tag header on the feed response would explain it, and would also mean the RNLI is deliberately keeping crawlers off the feed. (4) The repo's own merged bundle from agent-eight says the rnli.org RSS opened fine to the same tool on 15 Oct 2026, the day the watch got 403, which points at client filtering rather than a dead address. (5) Terms: clause 7.2 permits printing and downloading extracts for personal non-commercial use; clause 7.3 requires written permission for any other use; nothing mentions RSS or automated access. The watch stores only links, dates, a derived kind and a headline hash, but a reviewer should decide whether hourly automated reading needs the RNLI's permission; asking the press office for feed access would settle both the terms and the 403 at once. (6) Lifeboat launches: the RNLI publishes a pager-driven 'Latest lifeboat launches' page (station and launch time, last 48 hours) with no feed or API address visible in the rendered page; the JSON it loads is only visible in a browser's network tab. Historical call-outs (abridged 2021-2025 returns of service) are on the RNLI open-data portal under the GIS Open Data Licence, which requires the attribution 'Contains Open Data licensed under the GIS Open Data Licence.' Precisely what could not be established: whether the feed returns items at all today; the newest item date; whether a browser User-Agent alone cures the 403 or whether the runner's address is also blocked. A person with a browser can open the feed address, confirm it renders XML and the newest date, then from a laptop run the watch's fetch with its own user agent and with a browser user agent to split the two causes. No repository file was modified.
